blocks.text: The angriest reviews in this corpus stop describing and start commanding: VAROKAA HUIJAUSTA, älkää menkö tänne, älä usko. This is the imperative mood — and its negative form leans directly on the negation family you already know from Lesson 3.

blocks.title: Shouting in written form
blocks.text: When a Finnish reviewer switches to imperative — and often to capital letters, like VAROKAA HUIJAUSTA — it's a clear tonal shift from personal complaint to public warning. They're no longer just describing their own bad experience; they're issuing an instruction to every future reader. It's one of the strongest moves a review can make.

blocks.content: A plural command (addressing 'you all', including the polite formal 'you') adds {-kaa|grammar|imperative plural suffix|command, you all} or -kää to the verb stem. Varoa (to beware) → {varokaa|grammar|imperative, plural|beware!}. This is a direct, one-word instruction — no subject pronoun needed.

To say 'don't', Finnish uses a negation word just like en/ei/eivät from Lesson 3 — but in a special imperative form. {Älä|grammar|negative imperative, singular|do not (you)} is for one person, {älkää|grammar|negative imperative, plural|do not (you all)} for several or for formal address. Exactly like ei toimi, the main verb after älä/älkää loses its normal ending and takes the bare connegative form: mennä (to go) → älkää {menkö|grammar|connegative|go}.

items.fi: {Älä|grammar|negative imperative, singular|do not} usko, jos korjaamo väittää vastaan.
items.en: Don't believe it if the repair shop claims otherwise.

blocks.text: Piece 3 — Same family as en, ei, eivät

blocks.title: One negation system, three moods
blocks.text: En (I don't), ei (it doesn't), älä/älkää (don't! — command) are all part of the same negation-verb family from Lesson 3. In every case, the negation word carries the person, and the main verb drops down to its bare connegative stem: en suosittele, ei toimi, älkää menkö — same shape, three different jobs.

items.fi: {Älkää|grammar|negative imperative, plural|do not} {ikinä|word|adverb|ever} {viekö|grammar|connegative|take} tänne pienimpäänkään korjaukseen.
items.en: Never take it here for even the smallest repair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Is it worth taking the car to that repair shop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Ei missään nimessä. Älkää menkö tänne!

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Varokaa huijausta — älä usko, vaikka he väittävät vastaan.
lines.en: Beware of fraud — don't believe it, even if they claim otherwise.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: You don't need to learn älä and älkää as brand new words. They're just en and eivät's cousins, wearing a command hat. If you can already build ei toimi, you can build älkää menkö the exact same way — negation word first, bare verb stem second.

blocks.content: Älkää: ÄL-kää (the 'ä' is like 'a' in 'cat', double 'ää' held long — this word is often the loudest in a warning review). Menkö: MEN-kö (short, sharp — the 'ö' rounds your lips slightly, like German 'ö'). Varokaa: VA-ro-kaa (three syllables, long final 'aa').

rows.en: go (connegative of mennä, used after älä/älkää)
take (connegative of viedä, used after älä/älkää)
